result.topic_en: The page puts a differential equation into a series-integrable form, works a numerical example of the arithmetic-geometric mean of 3 and 1 taken with an imaginary (negative-root) branch, and sketches the key step of a proof that the AGM series satisfy a common second-order differential equation, giving a Wronskian-type relation.

methods.what: Rewriting a differential equation in a form integrable by series
AGM iteration of 3 and 1 with complex values (negative branch of the square root), carried out in logarithms and arguments in degrees
methods.quote: Beispiel für einen imaginären Werth des A. G. Mittels

methods.what: Relation between the reciprocal of a non-principal AGM value and the principal values
Hypergeometric series for the reciprocal AGM, m/λ, in terms of a = n/m (and B in the complementary modulus b)
Second-order linear differential equation satisfied by A, and also by B as a function of a
Wronskian of the two solutions: (a^3-a) times the Wronskian is constant
